info.title: Speckle Server REST API
info.description: REST API for Speckle Server. The object endpoints serve object graphs on every Speckle server, including the open-source server. The bundle and properties endpoints exist on Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, not on the open-source server.

servers.description: Self-hosted instance (replace with your server URL)

bearerAuth.description: Personal access token. Get your token from your Speckle profile settings.

ObjectId.description: A unique identifier for a Speckle object

ObjectIdArray.description: A JSON-serialized array of object IDs

ObjectDiffResponse.description: A dictionary mapping object IDs to boolean values indicating whether the server already has that object

post.summary: Check if the Server Contains a List of Objects
post.description: This method is useful for optimizing uploads, so that objects that are already in the project are not uploaded for every commit. Returns a dictionary mapping object IDs to boolean values indicating whether each object exists on the server. On Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, this endpoint no longer checks existence: it reports every object as absent, so clients upload their full graph. Speckle Cloud removes it on 26 November 2026 (announced with a `Sunset` header). On the open-source Speckle Server it is current.

200.description: Dictionary mapping object IDs to boolean values

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing authentication token

x-mint.content:
<Warning>
  Deprecated on Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, where it reports every object as absent. Speckle Cloud removes it on 26 November 2026. Current on the open-source Speckle Server.
</Warning>

## Limits

*Recommended* max number of objects to check: `1000`

post.description: Upload a batch of objects to a project. The batch is sent as multipart-encoded file content. Multiple batches can be sent in the same request as multiple files. On Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, this endpoint is deprecated: every response carries `Deprecation` and `Warning` headers, and it writes object graphs only. On the open-source Speckle Server it is current. To publish to Speckle Cloud, publish through ingestions instead.

file.description: JSON file containing an array of objects, optionally gzip-compressed

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing authentication token

413.description: Payload too large - Request exceeds 50 MB limit

x-mint.content:
<Warning>
  Deprecated on Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, where it writes object graphs only. On Speckle Cloud, [publish through ingestions](/developers/migration/publish-through-ingestions) instead. Current on the open-source Speckle Server.
</Warning>

## Notes

- The server accepts multiple batches as multiple files in the same call
- It's recommended to compress the batch with gzip and set the uploaded file `content_type` to `application/gzip`
- Otherwise, set it to `application/json`

## Limits

- Maximum size of each individual object: `10 MB` (large objects can be split into multiple objects using `chunkable` properties and `detachable` properties)
- Maximum size of each request: `50 MB` hard limit

get.description: Download a single object by its ID. Returns only the specified object without its children. Public projects need no token. On Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, this endpoint is deprecated: every response carries `Deprecation` and `Warning` headers, and it serves object-graph versions only. On the open-source Speckle Server it is current. A bundle reference (`bundle.<projectId>.<modelId>.<versionId>`) returns **404** with `error: "BUNDLE_REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND"`: read bundle versions with the artifacts endpoints instead.

parameters.name: objectId
parameters.description: The ID of the object to download

200.description: The JSON representation of the object

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing authentication token

404.description: No such object, or the object id is a bundle reference (`BUNDLE_REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND`).

</Warning>

post.description: Download multiple objects by their IDs. This method is useful when optimizing downloads: Get the root object without children, check the children ids in the local cache and then request only the new objects with this method. The response format depends on the Accept header. On Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, this endpoint is deprecated: every response carries `Deprecation` and `Warning` headers, and it serves object-graph versions only. On the open-source Speckle Server it is current. A bundle reference (`bundle.<projectId>.<modelId>.<versionId>`) returns **404** with `error: "BUNDLE_REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND"`: read bundle versions with the artifacts endpoints instead.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Response format: 'application/json' returns a JSON array, 'text/plain' returns tab-separated values (object_id\tobject_content)

200.description: The requested objects. Format depends on Accept header.

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing authentication token

x-mint.content:
<Warning>
  Deprecated on Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, where it serves object graphs only. Current on the open-source Speckle Server. To read a bundle version, use the [bundle endpoints](/developers/api/rest#bundle-endpoints).
</Warning>

## Limits

*Recommended* max number of objects to download with 1 request: `1000`

## Response Format

- If `Accept` is `text/plain`, each line of the output contains 1 object in the format: `{object_id}\t{object_content}`
- If `Accept` is `application/json`, the output is a JSON representation of an array of objects.

get.summary: Download an Object and All its Children
get.description: Download an object and all of its children recursively. The response format depends on the Accept header. Public projects need no token. On Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later, this endpoint is deprecated: every response carries `Deprecation` and `Warning` headers, and it serves object-graph versions only. On the open-source Speckle Server it is current. A bundle reference (`bundle.<projectId>.<modelId>.<versionId>`) returns **404** with `error: "BUNDLE_REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND"`: read bundle versions with the artifacts endpoints instead.

parameters.description: The ID of the root object to download

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Response format: 'application/json' returns a JSON array, 'text/plain' returns tab-separated values (object_id\tobject_content)

get.description: Returns a presigned GET URL, valid for one hour, for every file of a bundle version. Fetch the files from storage directly. Public projects need no token; others need read access, and a token's resource access rules must cover the model or version. Versions older than the workspace plan's history limit are refused. Available on Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later; not on the open-source Speckle Server.

200.description: A presigned GET URL per bundle file.

name.description: The file name, such as `<versionId>.eav.eav.parquet`. Match files by the end of the name.

url.description: Presigned GET URL. Fetch it without the Authorization header.

geometryStream.description: Present when the bundle has a viewer `.dat` file: the server-relative path of the geometry-stream WebSocket.

401.description: No valid token for a non-public project.

403.description: The token cannot read this project, model or version, or the version is beyond the workspace history limit.

404.description: No such project or version, or the version is not a bundle.

post.description: Exports every indexed property of every object in the version, one row per property, as JSON, CSV or Parquet, as a file attachment. JSON and CSV are gzip-encoded when `Accept-Encoding` includes gzip; Parquet never is. The body takes no filters. Public projects need no token; others need read access, and a token's resource access rules must cover the model or version. Versions older than the workspace plan's history limit are refused. Available on Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later; not on the open-source Speckle Server. Serves object-graph versions only: a bundle version returns **404** with `"Version not found or has no EAV artefact"`; read its properties from the bundle's `eav` files instead.

200.description: The properties, as a file attachment.

401.description: No valid token for a non-public project.

403.description: The token cannot read this project, model or version, or the version is beyond the workspace history limit.

404.description: No such project or version, or the version has no properties database (bundle versions).

get.description: Streams the version's properties as a DuckDB database: gzip-encoded when `Accept-Encoding` includes gzip (with `X-Estimated-Content-Length`), otherwise raw. Public projects need no token; others need read access, and a token's resource access rules must cover the model or version. Versions older than the workspace plan's history limit are refused. Available on Speckle Cloud and Speckle Enterprise Server 2026.9 and later; not on the open-source Speckle Server. Serves object-graph versions only: a bundle version returns **404** with `"Version not found or has no EAV artefact"`; read its properties from the bundle's `eav` files instead.

X-Estimated-Content-Length.description: Approximate gzip-encoded size, sent with gzip encoding.
